_doc: Two trace-level observations that feature replay could not have made.
The 2026-08-09 independent audit's point (section 5) was that
tools/validate_replay.py verifies DERIVED FEATURES rather than archived
voltage, so a trace that is wrong in the same way twice reproduces perfectly.
tools/retain_waveforms.py retains a stratified sample of actual waveforms and
runs a battery of checks features cannot express. It was run over 445 samples
spanning 8 models x 3 regimes x campaign blocks plus the risk strata already
The primary result is positive and worth stating first: 23,413 features
recomputed from the RETAINED VOLTAGE match their stored values exactly, with
zero mismatches. The archived trace really does regenerate the stored row.
Two things the battery found that the campaign's own QC does not flag are
recorded below. NEITHER has been repaired, and that is deliberate: the QC
thresholds are frozen properties of the campaign, and moving one after seeing
which samples it admits is an outcome-driven change that would also invalidate
every stored shard. They are reported with their measured prevalence so a
reader can judge them, and so a future campaign can set the bounds before

what: 8 of 445 retained traces (1.8%) leave the [-150, +80] mV band on the
hyperpolarising step. All 8 are khaliq_purkinje, the model with by far the
highest input resistance in the panel (median 593 MOhm, 99th percentile
2,361 MOhm, against a median of 23-49 MOhm for every other model). At a
fixed -0.05 nA step this is Ohm's law, not a numerical failure.
gap: The campaign's own QC flag `nonphysical_voltage` fires when V leaves
[-150, +80]. Six of the eight already carry the QC flag and are
analysis_eligible=False. TWO fall in the 10 mV gap between the two lower
khaliq_purkinje E1 sample 500: V_min = -158.2 mV, class 'spontaneous'
khaliq_purkinje E2 sample  58: V_min = -152.8 mV, class 'spontaneous'
prevalence: 2 of 445 retained samples (0.45%) are eligible AND breach -150 mV.
A campaign-wide count is NOT available: the trace minimum is not a stored
column, and a steady-state estimate from the stored input resistance
(V_rest + I*R_in) predicts 204 eligible khaliq rows below -150 mV of which
ALL carry the QC flag -- i.e. the steady-state estimate misses precisely
the marginal transient cases these two are. The 0.45% is therefore a
measurement on the retained sample, not an extrapolation.
consequence: Affects features measured against the hyperpolarising step -- input
resistance, sag ratio, sag amplitude, membrane tau. A model driven to
-158 mV is being measured far outside the range its channel kinetics were
fitted in; the number is a correct measurement of the model and not of
anything biological. It does not affect the step_abs_hi spike features that
carry most of the conditioning phenotype.
not_repaired: Tightening `nonphysical_voltage` to -150 mV would change the accepted
ensembles and require regenerating all 130,098 simulations, and choosing
the bound now, having seen which samples it excludes, is exactly the
outcome-driven adjustment the sensitivity cascade exists to prevent. A
future campaign should set the hyperpolarising amplitude per model from
measured input resistance rather than as a fixed absolute current.

what: 31 of 445 retained samples (7.0%) show the pre-stimulus mean still moving
when the step arrives: |mean(last 50 ms before onset) - mean(earlier
pre-stimulus)| exceeds 10% of the trace's total voltage excursion.
Distributed across five models: pospischil_rs 13, pospischil_fs 10,
gap: This is a DIFFERENT defect from the one QC catches. The `unstable_baseline`
flag fires when the peak-to-peak range of the second half of the
that is a ripple detector. A membrane settling smoothly toward its resting
potential has a small peak-to-peak inside any short window while its MEAN
is still moving, so it passes the ripple test and fails this one. 28 of the
43 flagged protocol-instances carry no `unstable_baseline` flag, and their
consequence: This is the same failure mode already documented for ortner_snc_da under
gate N6, where an unsettled baseline plus an Ih sag produced a NEGATIVE
input resistance. Every feature defined relative to a pre-stimulus
baseline -- input resistance, sag, resting potential -- inherits the drift.
The affected fraction is small and the drift is bounded at ~10-20% of the
response excursion in the observed cases.
not_repaired: The fix is a longer pre-stimulus settling period, which changes
protocol_hash and therefore every shard identity. Recorded here as a known
limitation of the frozen protocol; the next campaign should measure the
settling time per model and set DELAY_MS from it.

what_this_does_not_show: Nothing here is a reproduction failure. Zero of 23,413 recomputed features
disagreed with their stored values, and no retained trace contained a NaN, an
Inf, a spike of implausible shape, an undetected depolarisation block, or a
discontinuity larger than the integrator can produce in one step.
The sample is 445 of 130,098 simulations. It is stratified to cover every
model, regime and campaign block and to over-sample the risky strata, but a
defect confined to a few hundred ordinary samples could still be missed.
